subject: GPU exposure ladder & deal safeguards / ops play
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia@stellarishealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Jake Turner <jake.turner@stellarishealth.com>, procurement@stellarishealth.com
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on reserve term / GPU price exposure

Marcus — thanks for the call earlier. Jake and I are drafting internal notes for procurement and need one clear ask from Redwood: how would you structure a reserved capacity agreement so Stellaris isn’t over-exposed if GPU spot/market prices spike? Two specific asks: (1) can we get a small price protection construct for the first 12 months tied to an external GPU index, and (2) what options exist if we want to reduce committed quantity after month 6 without a heavy clawback?

We saw references on your side to "exposure ladders" and "credit escrows" — can you share a short playbook and the approvals path? We need this to present to our CFO on Monday.

Attachments: (1) draft-RFP-stellaris.pdf (we attached the RFP they shared)

Thanks,
Olivia Park
Head of Product, Stellaris Health

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 09:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on reserve term / GPU price exposure

Olivia — great questions, and thanks for flagging the Monday timeline. Below is a concise playbook that balances Stellaris's desire for downside protection with Redwood's need to plan fleet capacity. I attached an illustrative spreadsheet (gpu_exposure_ladder_v1.xlsx) with numbers we can tweak.

High-level proposal (summary):
- Exposure ladder (three tiers):
  * Tier 1 (0-60% of committed): fully guaranteed price (base discount) with no clawback window for months 0–6.
  * Tier 2 (61-85%): conditional discount + 30-day buffer; if market GPU index moves > +20% vs baseline, Stellaris receives a pro-rated credit from a short-term escrow pool.
  * Tier 3 (86-100% capacity): flexible buffer — Redwood can reassign up to 14% of capacity to a burst pool with 30 days notice; Stellaris receives a preferential reclaim window if prices stabilize.
- Credit escrow: a modest escrow funded by Redwood (or split) sized to cover typical 90th-percentile index shocks; released on predefined triggers.
- Decommit window: one-sided, limited reduction allowed at month 6 up to 10% of committed capacity if a documented usage shortfall is demonstrated; reductions beyond that trigger a pro-rated fee or conversion to an On-demand buffer credit.
- Pricing trigger: tied to public GPU index (we propose the "GPI-Global" index) with a transparent formula.

Approval path & timelines we recommend:
1) Sales + Finance (Karthik & David) sign off on discounting and escrow sizing — target 48 hours.
2) Legal review on contract language for trigger definitions and decommit mechanics — target 3 business days.
3) Marissa to approve any exec-level concession > $400k term exposure.

Next steps I suggest:
- Karthik, can you populate the attached sheet with a sensitivity table showing net effective $/token at +/-10/20/40% GPU index moves?
- David, please advise whether Finance can approve an escrow up to $350k pre-seed (or do we need exec approval).
- Olivia/Jake, if this looks directionally right I can draft a short term-addendum for you to review and we can run Legal in parallel.

Thanks — attaching the ladder spreadsheet and a one-page summary (stellaris_term_outline.pdf).

Best,
Marcus
Senior Director, Sales — Dedicated & Strategic
Redwood Inference

Thanks, Marcus. I ran several sensitivity scenarios and populated gpu_exposure_ladder_v1.xlsx with three example purchase bands and the resulting net-effective $/GPU-hour at index deltas of -10%, +10%, +25%, and +40%. Key notes: 
- At +25% index move the escrow covers ~65% of a worst-case shortfall at the Tier 2 level for the mid-sized commitment in the sheet.
- To keep the commercial math simple for procurement, we recommend two approval thresholds: (A) auto-approve by Finance for escrow up to $250k; (B) any escrow > $250k requires Marissa (sales leadership) + Finance SVP sign-off.

A few operational asks so we can scope:
1) Which fleet pool would Stellaris be pinned to? (aurora-dedicated vs reserved-flex). We propose starting them on reserved-flex to allow some operational rebalancing while honoring latency SLOs.
2) Do they need a hard region pin? (they are US-first; we can suggest a primary us-west region with cross-region fallback).
3) If we include a 6-month conditional decommit for up to 10% of capacity, Legal will want objective usage tests (e.g., 14-day rolling average under X% of committed peak).

Links: sensitivity sheet (Drive) -> https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3Cgx-GPU-Exposure-Ladder

Olivia — if that approval path works for Stellaris, I can prepare the commercial addendum and a short redline checklist for Legal. Marcus — David, can you confirm Finance auto-approve threshold?

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal, Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

Team — thank you for moving quickly. High level: I approve proceeding with the exposure ladder construct and the proposed two-tier approval for escrow sizing (Finance auto-approve to $250k; anything above that comes to me + Finance SVP).

Operational caveats for Sales to document in the addendum:
- Clear index source and fallback (we prefer GPI-Global + vendor verification clause).
- Explicit monitoring windows and SLAs for reclaiming capacity; avoid open-ended language.
- A fixed definition of "usage shortfall" for the 6-month decommit that is programmable (14-day rolling average < 55% of committed peak).

Marcus — once you send the first draft addendum to Olivia, loop Legal and Finance with the spreadsheet. If escrow > $400k I want a cover memo summarizing strategic rationale.

Marissa Cole
VP Sales — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
